title: Russia and Ukraine Trade Overnight Airstrikes as Brussels Talks on Reconstruction Resume
dek: Strikes hit the Kyiv area and other Ukrainian regions overnight as diplomats prepared to discuss postwar reconstruction and security guarantees in Brussels.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The U.S. Capitol, west front (file photo)

keyPoints: Russia and Ukraine exchanged damaging airstrikes overnight into Thursday, the Associated Press reported.
AP reported a warehouse fire in Sofiivska Borshchahivka on the outskirts of Kyiv after a Russian drone attack.
Talks on Ukraine's postwar reconstruction and security guarantees were set to resume in Brussels on Thursday, according to the AP.
Trump predicted a "very big" agreement with Russia after meeting Dmitriev, the Guardian reported.
Zelenskyy said every Ukrainian power plant has been damaged by attacks, the Guardian reported.
body:
Russia and Ukraine exchanged airstrikes overnight into Thursday, Nov. 5, as diplomats prepared to resume talks in Brussels on Ukraine's postwar reconstruction and on the security guarantees that would follow an end to the war, the Associated Press reported.

## Overnight strikes

AP photographs from Thursday showed a firefighter working at a destroyed warehouse in Sofiivska Borshchahivka, on the outskirts of Kyiv, after what the agency described as a Russian drone attack. The AP's reporting describes the overnight exchange as damaging on both sides.

The AP's account frames the strikes as part of a wider pattern of attacks that has continued even as diplomacy moves forward. The AP's reporting does not give overnight casualty figures. Separately, Zelensky said 43 people have been confirmed killed in a Russian strike on Monday in Komyshuvakha, near the front line in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, as rescue teams searched for more than 30 people believed trapped in the wreckage of a former school and a nearby shelter, the AP reported. Kremlin-installed officials in Luhansk said a Ukrainian attack killed five people and wounded 13 on a bus, with further details not immediately available.

## Talks in Brussels

The Brussels discussions focus on reconstruction and security guarantees after the war ends, not on a ceasefire. Those are separate questions from the immediate military situation, and the talks are set to resume on the same day the strikes were reported.

Separately, Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty reported that US special envoy Steve Witkoff said Washington would bring Ukrainian and Russian delegations together in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11 for working-level talks. That date comes from the RFE/RL reporting and has not been independently confirmed in the AP coverage reviewed for this story.

## What is not yet known

The reporting reviewed for this story does not say whether the Brussels talks will produce any agreement, whether the Abu Dhabi meeting will go ahead as scheduled, or what security guarantees either side would accept. Meridian will update this story if the AP or other reporting establishes new facts.

## Background

The overnight exchange comes nearly five years after Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, which the AP describes as the conflict the Brussels discussions are meant to bring to an end. The Washington Times reported that both sides launched hundreds of missiles and drones at critical targets overnight, as diplomats prepared for the technical talks over Kyiv's reconstruction. Those figures come from that outlet's reporting and have not been independently verified by Meridian.

The talks in Brussels are technical in nature. They concern how Ukraine would be rebuilt and what security assurances might look like once fighting stops. Neither the AP nor the other outlets reviewed for this story describe a ceasefire agreement being finalized this week, and none of the reporting reviewed here attributes the overnight strikes to a specific decision by either government's leadership.

Meridian is treating the strikes and the talks as separate stories: the airstrikes are reported events from overnight, while the Brussels and Abu Dhabi meetings are scheduled discussions whose outcomes are not yet known.

## Trump predicts a "very big" deal

On Thursday, after an unscheduled meeting with Kirill Dmitriev, Putin's envoy, at the White House, Trump said he expected "a big agreement" that "is going to involve more than Ukraine," the Guardian reported. Trump said he had not met the Ukrainian officials who were also at the White House that day, the Guardian reported.

At a summit in Madrid, Zelenskyy said "every power plant in Ukraine has been damaged in one way or another by attacks" and asked Latin American partners for grid equipment, the Guardian reported. Russia's Defense Ministry said its forces shot down nearly 500 Ukrainian drones overnight, according to the Business Mirror, which carried an AP report.
